items.title: What's New @ NAFA August 2026
items.author: Hung Ching Wen, Annie
items.description:
New Initiatives in Creative Health & Cultural Policy
NAFA launched two new initiatives in July and August, dedicated to advancing research, practice and partnerships across cultural policy, the creative industries, arts, wellbeing and society.
On 28 July 2026, NAFA launched the Centre for Creative Health, an interdisciplinary initiative advancing research, practice and partnerships at the intersection of the arts, wellbeing and society. Bringing together expertise across the arts, education, healthcare and the community, the Centre aims to contribute Asian perspectives to the growing field of Creative Health.
Read more about it here! ->
Centre for Creative Health
This was followed by the launch of the Cultural Policy Lab on 5 August 2026, a new initiative dedicated to research on cultural policy, arts ecosystems and the creative industries in Singapore and Southeast Asia. The Lab strengthens NAFA’s research capabilities and its contribution to broader conversations on the arts, culture and society.
Read more about it here! ->
Cultural Policy Lab
Margins & Methods for Inclusive Worlds
A gathering of senses and stories, intimate yet exuberant. Across performances, participation and dialogue, the Forum brought sound, movement, touch, sight and emotion into one room, creating a shared experience of discovery, connection and response.
UOB-NAFA Southeast Asian Arts Forum, held on 12 August 2026, explored neurodiversity, access, care, and more inclusive forms of participation across education, culture, and the arts. Bringing together artists and designers whose practices were shaped by neurodiverse realities, the Forum examined how sensory-led approaches across sound, movement, image, material, performance, and interactive media could offer alternative ways of understanding perception, participation, and belonging.
Through these practices, the Forum invited audiences to question established norms and consider new possibilities for access, translation, care, and engagement in the arts. Continue the conversation by sharing your thoughts and reflections through the post-event survey.
Read more about it here! ->
UOB-NAFA Southeast Asian Arts Forum
